stronger_finite_lemma.complete_type: For every j,D,q:Nat with1<=j and0<q, writing H_j(D)=sum_{u in Icc1D}(d_j(u):Real)/(u:Real), one has sum_{d in Icc1D}(d_j(d):Real)/(Nat.lcm d q:Real) <= ((d_(j+1)(q):Real)/(q:Real))*H_j(D). This also holds atD=0, with both sides0; no real Z is involved.
proof: For each1<=d<=D put g=gcd(d,q)>0 and u=d/g>0. Then g|q,d=g*u and gcd(u,q/g)=1. The latter is the exact residual coprimality; do NOT replace it with gcd(u,q)=1, which can be false. Since gcd(g*u,q)=g, lcm(d,q)=q*u. Alsou<=d<=D.

The map d->(g,u) is injective because d=g*u. Its image is contained in q.divisors x Icc1D. By argument-submultiplicativity proved below, d_j(d)=d_j(g*u)<=d_j(g)*d_j(u). All denominators are positive, so d_j(d)/lcm(d,q)<=d_j(g)*d_j(u)/(q*u).

Sum over the injective image, then enlarge to the complete finite product q.divisors x Icc1D using nonnegative summands. This discards the residual coprimality and the sharper gu<=D restriction only in an upper bound. The resulting sum factors EXACTLY as (1/q)*(sum_{g|q}d_j(g))*H_j(D).
The actual fouvryTau_succ j q gives sum_{g|q}d_j(g)=d_(j+1)(q). This proves the finite inequality with precisely the requested constant, not a tau(q) surrogate or extra log.
stronger_finite_lemma.optional_exact_gcd_fiber_identity: The original sum equals (1/q)*sum_{g|q}sum_{1<=u<=floor(D/g),gcd(u,q/g)=1}d_j(g*u)/u. This is mathematically exact; formalizing the injection bound above is smaller because it avoids constructing a full fiber bijection.

argument_submultiplicativity.new_lemma_type: theorem fouvryTau_mul_argument_le {j m n : Nat} (hj : 1<=j) (hm : 0<m) (hn : 0<n) : fouvryTau j (m*n) <= fouvryTau j m * fouvryTau j n
argument_submultiplicativity.not_existing_mul_le: Actual native fouvryTau_mul_le(k,l,n) states d_k(n)*d_l(n)<=d_(k*l)(n). It has one integer argument and two orders. Neither its direction nor its parameters proves the new lemma. Multiplicativity only gives equality for coprime m,n and also does not suffice alone.
complete_recursive_proof: Induct on j starting at1. For positive m,n, native fouvryTau_order_one makes all three order-one values1, so the base is equality.

Suppose the assertion holds at j for all positive arguments. For each e|(m*n), put b=gcd(e,m),c=e/b. Then b|m and c|n, and both are positive. To see c|n, write e=b*c,m=b*m1. The identity gcd(c,m1)=1 and e|m*n imply c|m1*n by cancellation of positive b; Euclid's lemma gives c|n. Equivalently, lcm(e,m)|m*n and lcm(e,m)=m*c give c|n. No coprimality of c and m is asserted.

The divisor map e->(b,c) is injective by e=b*c. The inductive hypothesis yields d_j(e)<=d_j(b)*d_j(c). Enlarge its nonnegative weighted image to all b|m,c|n. Thus sum_{e|mn}d_j(e)<=sum_{b|m,c|n}d_j(b)*d_j(c).

Apply native fouvryTau_succ on each side and finite product-sum factorization. The result is d_(j+1)(mn)<=d_(j+1)(m)*d_(j+1)(n), closing the induction. This proof uses only positive-divisor arithmetic, finite injections and the existing successor recurrence.

existing_exact_API_references.type: def fouvryTau (k : Nat) : ArithmeticFunction Nat := ArithmeticFunction.zeta ^ k
theorem fouvryTau_order_one {n : Nat} (hn : n != 0) : fouvryTau 1 n = 1
theorem fouvryTau_succ (k n : Nat) : fouvryTau (k+1) n = sum d in n.divisors, fouvryTau k d
theorem sum_fouvryTau_div_le (k N : Nat) : (sum n in Ioc0N, (fouvryTau k n:Real)/n) <= (1+Real.log N)^k
theorem sum_fouvryTau_div_le_real (k : Nat) {x : Real} (hx : 1<=x) : (sum n in Ioc0(floor x), (fouvryTau k n:Real)/n) <= (1+Real.log x)^k
